title: One NFIP Building Policy per Building — NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
The National Flood Insurance Program allows only one NFIP building policy on a building, and the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) apply that rule as follows.

1. **Issue condition.** A new building policy is issued only when no other General Property Form or RCBAP policy with building coverage at the same property address is in status pending effective, in force or renewal grace.
2. **Unit policies.** A non-residential condominium unit policy can coexist with the association's RCBAP on the same building because it insures only the unit owner's interest.
3. **Duplicates.** When two building policies on the same building are found in force, the one with the later original effective date is the duplicate and is cancelled under the reason duplicate NFIP policy.
4. **No stacking.** Limits are never added across duplicate policies.

## Evidence

The check reads Tidemark's own policy records for the same property address: whether another policy there carries building coverage and whether its status is pending effective, in force or renewal grace. What a caller says about other cover does not replace those records.

## Cases (hypothetical)

| Records at the property address | New building policy |
|---|---|
| No other General Property Form or RCBAP policy with building coverage | may be issued |
| Another such policy in force | not issued |
| Another such policy in renewal grace | not issued |
| Another such policy pending effective | not issued |
| Another such policy cancelled or lapsed | the rule's bar does not arise from that policy |
| Only a non-residential condominium unit policy, and the new policy is the association's RCBAP | may coexist |

Where two building policies are found in force on one building, the policy whose original effective date is later is the one cancelled as the duplicate, and its limits are never combined with the other's.
